sources.supports: Primary structural reference for continuity between synthesized RNA and its polymerase-bound growing end; polymerase-family-specific protein architecture is not transferred to the bacterial schematic.

findings.evidence: The lactose-dependent release starts at p=.17, while both bound ligand meshes remain invisible until p=.25. At p=.24 LacI has moved 0.5363 world units from its original operator pose; at p=.249 it has moved 0.6594, still with no drawn inducer occupancy.
findings.whyWrong: The specific induction animation reverses its own stated allolactose-binding -> lower operator affinity -> induced dissociation order. This is a deterministic ligand-conditioned release, not a depiction of stochastic basal dissociation.
findings.fix: Complete the ligand-binding event before starting the modeled LacI induction displacement, retaining no-lactose repression and both glucose branches.
findings.verification: Assert the actual repressor world pose remains at its bound starting pose until its allolactose meshes show occupancy; then assert continuous departure and later transcription across both lactose-present branches.

findings.location: 225-245; structuralDetails.js duplex update and nascentBridge visibility
findings.evidence: Across p±1e-6 at six RNAP entry/release boundaries, individual DNA phosphate jumps reach 0.2037–0.6738 world units. At .87/.91/.95 a visible RNA bridge of length 1.0698/1.4045/1.7487 disappears outright; the 3-prime end location changes by 0.9884/1.3421/1.6984.
findings.whyWrong: A binary polymerase visibility flag is reused as duplex opening and RNA bridge existence. Integration of twist carries the step down the DNA, while release removes a visibly long part of the same RNA chain instead of moving it continuously into the released conformation.
findings.fix: Use continuous opening/closing ramps and a continuous released-RNA transition that preserves the visible connected chain. Keep independent bubbles for all three RNAPs and exact arbitrary seeking.
findings.verification: Measure actual DNA instances around every entry/release with decreasing epsilon; verify displacement tends to zero. Check the visible RNA endpoint/contour remains continuous through each release, not just the bridge.visible flag.

sources.title: Repression is relieved before attenuation in the trp operon of Escherichia coli as tryptophan starvation becomes increasingly severe.

sources.title: Attenuation in the Escherichia coli tryptophan operon: role of RNA secondary structure involving the tryptophan codon region.
sources.supports: Primary leader-transcript work supports alternative secondary structures within one connected trp leader RNA, coupled to ribosome behavior.

findings.evidence: Each following region starts .095 progress after the previous region begins, but the previous needs .12 progress to complete. At p=.513 in the antiterminator branch, region 4 is already visible (24 indices) while region 3 has only 1992/2112 indices. The upper-bound last visible tube-ring center remains .14837 units from the next region start, exceeding the sum of radii .104 by .04437. Thus the displayed single RNA is broken between regions.
findings.whyWrong: These colored regions are covalently contiguous portions of one transcript; simultaneous emergence of a downstream fragment before the preceding region reaches it misrepresents polymer-chain continuity. The final fully drawn paths do join, so endpoint-only tests miss the failure.
findings.fix: Reveal regions with a single ordered front or gate each downstream region until its predecessor reaches the junction. Preserve the two complete mutually exclusive RNA folds and draw nucleotide detail only over the connected visible prefix.
findings.verification: Inspect referenced drawn triangle rings and junction positions during each reveal transition in both branches/all four conditions. No nonempty downstream region may coexist with an incomplete predecessor.

findings.evidence: Across p=.2±1e-6 the DNA phosphate maximum displacement is .42720 world units. In high-Trp/normal-charging termination, p=.96±1e-6 yields .47891 displacement when the opening abruptly vanishes.
findings.whyWrong: The moving schematic transcription bubble changes from fully closed to fully open or back in one state switch; downstream integrated twist also changes instantly. This is a measurable internal-stage jump rather than the intentional player restart.
findings.fix: Drive bubble opening/closure with continuous event ramps tied to loading and release, preserving the initiated-transcript framing and readthrough outcome.
findings.verification: Numerically check actual DNA instance displacements at opening and terminating-release boundaries for both charged and stalled branches; no finite jump as epsilon shrinks.

findings.location: 277-292; binary DNA opening and RNA bridge visibility
findings.evidence: At p=.71±1e-6 active-branch DNA phosphate displacement reaches .44414; at p=.97±1e-6 it reaches .43114. The p=.97 release also removes a 1.05535-unit visible RNA exit bridge, moving the visible growing/released end by .97020 units. Other three control branches do not transcribe.

findings.verification: Check actual DNA instance motion and RNA chain endpoint/contour at .71 and .97, plus inactive controls and irregular seeks.

findings.location: 297-301 and 337-366; static glycerol positions versus shrinking membrane
findings.evidence: Glycerol groups remain in fixed world positions while only the plasma membrane shrinks/re-expands. In high-osmolarity/normal-Hog1 at p=.835, glycerol index 10 appears at [-2.3,-1.85,.08] while membrane scale is .876545. One actual atom center has outer-leaflet elliptical radius squared 1.06370; its rendered molecular surface reaches 1.10326. Values >1 put it outside the outer membrane ellipse, not in the cytoplasm. It remains partly outside until about p=.88.
findings.whyWrong: The scene labels these accumulating molecules as cytoplasmic glycerol retained by closed Fps1, but a newly produced molecule appears on/across the closed plasma membrane elsewhere. The fixed cell-wall outline does not make this location cytoplasmic.
findings.fix: Keep every visible glycerol molecule and its full geometry inside the current inner leaflet during shrinkage/recovery, by using cell-relative positions or a validated interior arrangement; preserve molecular scale/details and controls.
findings.verification: Across all four conditions and dense samples around each count activation, transform actual visible glycerol sphere/segment geometry into membrane-local coordinates and verify it stays strictly inside the inner leaflet with molecular-radius clearance.

findings: Hog1 piecewise path and volume ease are continuous; the confirmed issue is changing compartment containment, not a path teleport.
